chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu Hamza who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man says to his believing brother, 'Uff!', he exits from his Wilayah; and when he says, 'You are my enemy', one of the two has disbelieved; and Allah will not accept a deed from a believer while he is implicitly bearing ill-will against his believing brother.

key_terms.أُفٍّ: A minor expression of annoyance or impatience, indicating a level of disrespect.
key_terms.سُوءاً: Ill-wie/evil, referring to hidden animosity or malice in the heart.
key_terms.كَفَرَ: He disbelieved (kufr), indicating a potential state of major disbelief or apostasy in one of the parties.
key_terms.مُضْمِرٌ: He is concealing/harboring (internally), referring to hidden feelings.
key_terms.وَلَايَتِهِ: His Wilayah (guardianship, affinity, or spiritual connection), indicating a loss of close religious bond.

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual consequences of saying 'Uff' or 'You are my enemy' to a fellow Muslim?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish a hierarchy of spiritual severance based on the severity of verbal slight, ranging from the loss of mutual Wilayah for 'Uff' to potential Kufr for declaring enmity. This highlights the Shia emphasis on 'Mu'akhat' (brotherhood) as a covenantal bond where internalized animosity (ikhlad) invalidates outward worship, a concept deeply rooted in the ethical teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt.
